newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Folgado reiterates no need for mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Folgado reiterates no need for mini-budget.

text.p: Spanish Budget Secretary Jose Folgado reiterated on Wednesday that there was no need for a mini-budget later this year.
"The government is not planning any adjustment later in the year," Folgado told reporters.
If the macroeconomic forecast were to change, which is not currently expected, "the government would be ready to make the needed adjustment", given its commitment to fulfilling the deficit objective.
He presented a cash budget for February, on a cash basis, of 176.2 billion pesetas, which is 18.4 percent less than the year-ago figure of 216 billion pesetas.

At the same time, the February deficit on a national account basis, which is accumulated for the first two months, was at 286.5 billion pesetas, down 0.1 percent versus 286.8 billion peseta in February 1995.
Folgado added that two months was too short a period to assess the trend for the year.
